command:
set -euo pipefail
cd /tmp

echo "== verify staged inputs against their pinned sha256 (same proteome + queries as blast) =="
{ printf '%s  %s\n' 9b43da92651b35814597af6a8b18f500b768679a49fa4678224f384917ce7668 ensembl116_pep.fa.gz
  printf '%s  %s\n' e6732c4cf4fda1dd831e78cb9c0416c6357d6e462ec8ec75cac690801ab153a7 queries1000.fa
} > pins.sha256
sha256sum -c pins.sha256

# diamond makedb reads plain FASTA; gzip is a base-image utility, not a second tool
# (both steps here are diamond).
gzip -dc ensembl116_pep.fa.gz > pep.fa

echo "== diamond makedb: Ensembl 116 human proteome =="
diamond makedb --in pep.fa -d pepdb 2> makedb.log

echo "== diamond blastp --very-sensitive: 1000 queries vs the whole proteome =="
# --very-sensitive puts diamond in a sensitivity regime comparable to blastp's default.
# Comparing diamond's DEFAULT (fast) mode against blastp would be the like-with-like trap:
# different sensitivity modes return different hit sets for reasons unrelated to correctness
# (the same error as bowtie2 end-to-end vs --local). Match the modes, then compare.
T0=$(date +%s)
diamond blastp -q queries1000.fa -d pepdb \
  --outfmt 6 qseqid sseqid pident length qlen evalue bitscore \
  --very-sensitive --max-target-seqs 500 -p 4 -o dmnd_hits.tsv
T1=$(date +%s); SEARCH_S=$(( T1 - T0 )) 2> blastp.log

# ---- smoke check ----
# Same split blast's page arrived at the hard way: the EXACT claim is that a query which hits
# anything hits ITSELF at 100% identity; whether that self-alignment spans the whole query is
# data-dependent (blast loses 102 of 931 by exactly one residue). So both are measured, only the
# first is asserted, and the cross-code claim is the one both tools must satisfy.
#
# The cross-code metric is deliberately NOT "does diamond's top hit equal blast's top hit". On
# this query set many proteins are near-identical paralogs whose self-hit TIES on bitscore, and
# each tool breaks ties in its own order, so top-hit equality measures tie-breaking, not
# agreement. And diamond's heuristic bitscores differ from blastp's by design, so score equality
# is meaningless too. What both tools must agree on is the SET of self-hits recovered.
stats() { awk -F'\t' '
  { q[$1]=1 }
  $1==$2 { srow[$1]=1; if ($3+0==100) s100[$1]=1; if ($3+0==100 && $4==$5) full[$1]=1 }
  END { nq=0; ns=0; n1=0; nf=0
        for (k in q) nq++; for (k in srow) ns++; for (k in s100) n1++; for (k in full) nf++
        print nq" "ns" "n1" "nf }' "$1"; }
read DQH DSROW DS100 DFULL <<< "$(stats dmnd_hits.tsv)"
read BQH BSROW BS100 BFULL <<< "$(stats blast_hits.tsv)"
SHARED=$(awk -F'\t' 'FNR==NR{if($1==$2)b[$1]=1;next} $1==$2 && ($1 in b){print $1}' blast_hits.tsv dmnd_hits.tsv | sort -u | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
AGREE=$(awk -v s="$SHARED" -v b="$BSROW" 'BEGIN{printf "%.4f", (b>0? s/b : 0)}')
{
  echo "search_wall_s          $SEARCH_S   (diamond --very-sensitive, 16 threads)"
  echo "diamond_queries_hit    $DQH"
  echo "diamond_self_rows      $DSROW   want == diamond_queries_hit (EXACT)"
  echo "diamond_self_100pct    $DS100   want == diamond_self_rows (EXACT)"
  echo "diamond_full_len_self  $DFULL   OBSERVATION"
  echo "blast_queries_hit      $BQH   (same queries, same database)"
  echo "blast_self_rows        $BSROW"
  echo "self_hit_set_agreement $AGREE   want >= 0.95  (fraction of blast's self-hits diamond also finds)"
} > smoke-check.txt
cat smoke-check.txt
test "$DSROW" -eq "$DQH"
test "$DS100" -eq "$DSROW"
awk -v a="$AGREE" 'BEGIN{ if (a>=0.95) exit 0; print "self-hit set agreement " a " below 0.95"; exit 1 }'
echo "SMOKE CHECK PASSED"
